en: Regarding the *Verses on Amitābha Buddha* produced later, the ancient records state that the translator’s name is missing;
however, the current catalog of the Later Han period attributes it to the bhikṣu Weinianfa. It begins: "I have followed King Śirīṣa..."
He made vows comparable to those of all Buddhas, consisting of twenty-four chapters of oaths.
In life after life he beheld Buddhas, their number reaching immeasurable billions;
never abandoning his practices from past lives, his merit was thus fully perfected.
The world is named Pure, where a Buddha arises known as Immeasurable;
The realm is level and easy to traverse, abundant, joyful, and filled with superior beings.
Various kinds of jewel-trees grow in dense, orderly rows.
The roots, stems, branches, leaves, and flowers each emit various distinct fragrances.
Day by day, they stir three times with the wind; they unfold and bloom like flowers coming forth.
When they fall to the ground, they spread out as if laid by hand, intermingling so that the surface is everywhere level.
There were no mountains at all, nor oceans or springs;
there were only river currents, whose sounds were like the preaching of the sutras.
Gods and humans entered the water to play, according to whatever they desired.
The waters shall reach his shoulders, fulfilling every wish as it is conceived.
The Buddha’s lifespan shall equal the sands of the ten directions, and his radiance shall be universally boundless;
his bodhisattvas and disciples shall be beyond all calculation or measure.
If you wish to see that Buddha, do not doubt and do not forget;
if you harbor doubts within your womb, you shall not be united with him for five hundred years.
Without doubt, you shall take birth upon his seat, and with palms joined before the Immeasurable One.
Wishing to pervade the ten directions, he returns in an instant.
Contemplate that Bodhisattva, who for billions of kalpas performed diligent labors;
through such fundamental practice, he attained the title of World-Honored One.
The appearance of a Buddha is difficult to encounter; a momentary assembly to hear his teaching is rare to find.
A teacher who expounds the Dharma is hard to meet, and a disciple who receives instruction is difficult to obtain.
If one should later encounter the final age, when the Dharma is about to decline and fade away—
We shall together establish and uphold it, practicing the Buddha’s Dharma free from desire.
May the Buddha expound this essential teaching; may each person diligently contemplate and practice it.
Receiving this immeasurable merit, we shall bow our heads in reverence throughout every lifetime.
Verses on Amitābha Buddha Spoken Later on the Occasion of His Emergence from Samādhi
